prioritiesToday.text: URGENT -- Organisational Structure Update - August 2026 - FINAL
prioritiesToday.description:
orgstructure@admin.ox.ac.uk circulated a draft University PACS Organisational Structure update on 12 Aug 2026 (16:22 UTC), covering a wholesale move of College/Society entities from PACS level 2 to level 3, and a large Subsidiary Companies correction. On 17 Aug 2026 (10:22 UTC) Simon Burford (HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, HR Systems, People Department, simon.burford@admin.ox.ac.uk) forwarded the notice to Kevin, Christopher Sanders, James Salas Guillen, Michael O'Sullivan and David Johnson (cc Marie Cooksey, Sarah Rowles, Athena Artuso), assessing limited PeopleXD impact but proposing 3 new management units (0C01 Kellogg, 0C02 St Cross, 0C03 Reuben) to properly align the Societies area, and flagging a knock-on risk to org-structure mapping tables in the data warehouse -- specifically including the H&S mapping David Johnson and Christopher Sanders built for the H&S dashboard -- plus a possible HESA reporting impact (societies now returned for HESA). On 17 Aug 2026 (11:28 UTC) Sarah Rowles replied-all to Simon (cc Marie Cooksey, Athena Artuso; Kevin still a recipient) asking when this goes into the live environment, since dept code drives the Exemption Rules for the HESA Module and she has a full HESA generate (the last one) planned for Monday 24 August 2026; she noted Societies currently pass the Exemption Rules so should be unaffected, but flagged the rules may need updating for next year.

On 19 Aug 2026 (16:36) Katherine Corr (orgstructure@admin.ox.ac.uk) circulated the FINAL version, subject 'RE: Organisational Structure Update - August 2026 - FINAL', superseding the 12 Aug DRAFT. Changes are effective up to and including 19 Aug 2026. One correction made from the draft: a duplicate Oxuniprint Ltd subsidiary entity (XP) was removed; minor name changes were also made to entities 8HP0 and E7 at the relevant department's request. The full change schedule covers Medical Sciences, UAS, and Colleges/Halls (L2->L3 restructure), plus a wider Subsidiary Companies cleanup (deletions, renames, new entities). The latest file now lives on the intranet, migrated to SharePoint -- existing bookmarks need updating. System owners/admins of local systems (card database, Salto, Oracle etc.) need to reflect these changes and should log updates via the Teams group. As of the FINAL circulation, Simon Burford's PeopleXD/H&S-dashboard mapping question and Sarah Rowles' HESA go-live question (both raised 17 Aug in response to the draft) had not been answered in this thread. No reply from Kevin has been found in Sent Items as of the last live Outlook search (18 Aug).

prioritiesToday.text: URGENT -- Cority Applicant Data Import file (James Salas Guillen / Simon Burford thread)
prioritiesToday.description:
FULL RETRIEVAL (18 Aug 2026, Drew) -- HIGH PRIORITY / URGENT per Kevin's explicit instruction. This entry has been enriched with full verbatim email bodies (not paraphrases) specifically so Adam can cross-reference against the HR Functional Analysis Knowledge Base / CORITY-FEASIBILITY.md -- that cross-reference is Adam's domain, not assessed here.

THREAD IDENTITY: Outlook ConversationID E9A6B1561BB4476ABA498A3167C89560, subject "Cority - Applicant Data Import file" (no "Fw:"-prefixed variant of this subject was found live in Inbox, subfolders, or Sent Items -- searched case-insensitively with RE:/FW: prefix stripped across all 34 folders in the Inbox tree, incl. Inbox/H&S/Cority, plus Sent Items; Kevin has not replied on this thread -- zero matches in Sent Items). 5 messages total, all between James Salas Guillen (Senior Functional Analyst) and Simon Burford (HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager), addressed to/cc'ing Kevin throughout. A separate, unrelated earlier thread also titled just "Cority" (Marie Cooksey to James/Kevin, cc Christopher Sanders, 10 Apr 2026, different ConversationID B94B83BEB2CF4FA9A435E5A8BE527605, asking for an up/downstream system-impact schematic) surfaced in the same search but is NOT part of this chain -- noted for completeness only.

CHRONOLOGICAL FULL THREAD:

[1] 11 Aug 2026 13:11 UTC -- James Salas Guillen -> Kevin Lelitte, cc Simon Burford. Subject: "Cority - Applicant Data Import file".
Hi Kevin and Simon,

I wanted to provide an update on the Cority Applicant Data Import.

Following several uploads/imports in Production with real data, we've identified several formatting issues in the source report that require manual clean-up before the file can be successfully uploaded. These issues were not apparent during earlier testing and only became evident once we started processing production data.

The current report requires the following manual amendments before it can be uploaded to Cority:
1. Remove quotation marks from all fields (e.g. "First Name of Employee").
2. Ensure all column headers are contained within a single header row. Currently, the headers split across multiple rows when converted to CSV.
3. Format the Date of Birth field as a date only (dd/mm/yyyy) with no time component.
4. Ensure the file contains all 27 expected columns and corresponding headers even if no data is available.

Ideally, if the above changes can be implemented within the report itself, the report should be exported directly to CSV rather than Excel to eliminate the additional conversion and clean-up steps currently required.

As previously discussed, there may be an opportunity to implement these changes directly within the PXD reporting module, which would remove the need for ongoing manual work.

In addition, I have identified what appears to be a potential mismatch in the column mapping between our report and Cority. I currently have a support ticket open with the Cority support team to investigate this further. If the issue turns out to be on our side, we may also need to adjust the report column order accordingly.

Would it be possible to review whether these report changes can be made within PXD (RECSUP20_Applicant Cority Interface File)? Making these amendments at source would significantly reduce the manual effort required each time the file is processed for import.

Best wishes,
James Salas, Senior Functional Analyst, HR Systems | People Department | University of Oxford

[2] 18 Aug 2026 11:55 UTC -- Simon Burford replies (RE:).
Hi James,

I'm sure this is possible to do.

However, when I save the report as CSV and open it in notepad++ I see the following: [embedded screenshot -- see "Attachment note" below; the column headers to me look like they are in one row already, so how are you currently getting/viewing the CSV where it's split over multiple rows?]

Quotation marks in this file only exist where there is a comma in the data field, to prevent the columns breaking (e.g. in the screenshot above the division name "MATHS, PHYSICAL & LIFE SCIENCES" has a comma in it, so it adds quotes to stop the file interpreting MATHS as one column and PHYSICAL & LIFE SCIENCES as the next column). I'm assuming that this is expected behaviour and Cority can handle this?

The date of birth field is clearly an issue so this can hopefully be sorted, the headers are just the names of the text boxes but I have an idea of how this could be fixed so fingers crossed, but it definitely has commas denoting the columns even if the data is blank, so that should be fine.

Many thanks,
Simon Burford, HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, HR Systems | People Department | University of Oxford
ATTACHMENT NOTE: this message carries an embedded screenshot (image004.png, 48219 bytes) of the actual live file "RECSUP20_Applicant Cority Interface File_V1.csv" open in Notepad++. Opened and viewed directly (not just noted). The screenshot shows: (a) the current column headers are generic auto-generated names (Textbox7, Textbox3, Textbox5, Textbox9, Textbox11, Textbox15... at least 32 distinct Textbox-labelled columns visible), not human-readable labels -- corroborating both James's and Simon's header discussion; (b) REAL, LIVE APPLICANT PERSONAL DATA is visible in the data rows -- full names, dates of birth, home addresses, phone numbers, personal/institutional email addresses, and job/grade/department detail for multiple real individuals. This is production personal data, not test/dummy data. Deliberately NOT reproduced verbatim in this log entry (or anywhere else) beyond this structural description -- duplicating real applicants' PII into a second data store (this dashboard) was judged to add exposure risk without adding decision-useful value; the original screenshot remains only in the source Outlook message. Flagging the fact of real PII being screenshotted into an email thread for visibility, not assessing whether that itself is a concern -- that judgment belongs to Kevin/Adam, not Drew's retrieval role. All other attachments across this thread (13 total across the 5 messages) are repeated signature-logo images (17545/15482/3934/3395 bytes, byte-size-identical across every message) -- confirmed not distinct content. No actual .csv/.txt data file was ever attached as a real attachment anywhere in this thread -- only this one screenshot of it.

[3] 18 Aug 2026 13:02 UTC -- Simon Burford replies (RE:), follow-up questions.
Hi both,

Another couple of questions.

Do you need to retain the spaces in the column headings? Or would it be ok to have titles like Applicant_Number, Applicant_Title, First_name_of_employee etc?

Secondly, how was this report created? I can't see a copy of it on the QA server and I can't see a change request for it so it doesn't seem to have followed the standard approach to report development and deployment.

Many thanks,
Simon Burford

[4] 18 Aug 2026 16:41 UTC -- James Salas Guillen replies (RE:), answers inline ("in red" in the original -- colour is lost in plain-text export, reconstructed as attributed answers below).
Hi Simon,

Thank you very much for looking into this. I have added my responses in red [inline in the quoted message -- reconstructed below since plain-text export flattens colour]:

- On "do headers need to retain spaces / exact labels": "The column headings do not need to retain the spaces and do not necessarily need to have the exact labels. As long as the columns are in the correct order, the file should import correctly. The headings simply make it easier for us to diagnose any issues if the upload fails."
- On "how was this report created / not on QA server / no change request": "This is a question for @Kevin, as I do not have direct access to this report. At the moment, I have been relying on a member of the FA team to export it for me."
- On the notepad++ header-row discrepancy: "This issue appears to occur only when the Excel file is converted to CSV format, and the behaviour is not consistent. Hopefully, this will not be an issue when the dataset is exported directly to CSV from the PXD reporting module."
- On the quotation-marks-around-commas question: "This makes sense. However, the upload process currently flags this as an error. I'll raise this with the consultant during tomorrow's meeting to see whether there is anything we can do to address it."

Best wishes,
James Salas

[5] 18 Aug 2026 17:56 UTC -- Simon Burford replies (RE:) -- MOST RECENT MESSAGE, thread currently ends here, nothing further found live.
Thanks for the response James.

I am starting to think that it might be worth exploring if we can set up an automated export of a CSV to a file location. Do you have a network folder that you would want CSV files to be saved to? Presumably there's a location that is currently being used by whoever in the FA team is exporting the file now?

Two additional questions (sorry!)
1 - How does Cority want null values to be handled? I think there's different options for how null values can be exported, I'm pretty sure we could export as the following: [blank] / NULL / N/A / -. I think by default it's exporting as the first option, i.e. absolutely no value, but I would want to explicitly set the fields to do this if we were to set up some automated process, just in case the global defaults change, so please confirm.
2 - Does Cority expect UTF-8 encoding? This looks like the default encoding for automated CSV exports so just need to check that this is ok for Cority?

Upon further investigation it looks like Lee might have created the report and perhaps it was still in testing when he left? Although it seems to be being used as a live interface file, so I'm really not sure. @Kevin Lelitte if you have anything to add from what Lee handed over when he left that would be helpful.

Many thanks,
Simon Burford

STATUS: OPEN, unanswered by Kevin. Simon's message [5] contains two direct open questions plus an explicit @Kevin tag asking whether Kevin has anything from Lee's handover about how/why this report (RECSUP20_Applicant Cority Interface File) was created outside the standard QA/change-request process, given it's being used as a live production interface file. This is the specific pending decision/input needed from Kevin -- not a general "review" note.

CROSS-REFERENCE FLAG FOR ADAM: this report (RECSUP20_Applicant Cority Interface File) and its formatting/mapping issues sit squarely in the Cority H&S system expansion Adam tracks in CORITY-FEASIBILITY.md.
